basis: Origin is peritoneal fibroblastic tissue, outside the specified axes; involvement of a covered abdominal organ is not established.
An ocular motility disorder; a particular underlying neurologic disease is not established.
Defined by unequal pupils; neurologic injury cannot be inferred because physiologic and iris-related forms are included.
Psychiatric somatoform disorder without intrinsic organ damage.
Recurrent meningeal inflammation classified as viral meningitis, commonly associated with HSV-2.
Congenital cerebral aqueduct stenosis causes obstructive hydrocephalus.
Defined by craniofacial skeletal dysplasia and congenital cervical vertebral fusion; nasal appearance alone does not establish airway damage.
Scalp aplasia 10/11, enamel hypoplasia 9/9 and developmental delay 7/9 define the syndrome; cataracts affect 5/10.
Inherited nephrotic kidney disease; immune mechanisms and extrarenal damage are not shared across most subtypes.
Congenital pituitary malformation with hormone deficiencies; neurologic and optic abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Rickettsia japonica infection; acute rash and inoculation eschar do not establish common lasting skin dysfunction.
Disseminated Candida infection; organ seeding varies, with no specific organ established as commonly damaged across this umbrella.
Childhood epilepsy with characteristic EEG abnormalities and associated neuropsychological dysfunction.
The disease itself is chemotherapy-related peripheral nerve injury.
Metabolic encephalopathy; hepatic failure/cholestasis reported in 2/2, though sampling is small. VSD and enterocolitis each 1/2 are insufficiently established.
Skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly/ID and immunodeficiency define disease; cataracts 80-99%. Cap excludes enamel defects 80-99% and neutropenia 30-79%.
Congenital lower urinary tract obstruction; pulmonary hypoplasia is a complication of severe cases, not established across most patients.
Defined as inherited early-onset autoimmunity and immune dysregulation; supplied evidence does not establish frequent damage to a specific additional organ.
Ferritin deficiency affects iron storage; alopecia reported in 10/11. Blood-cell damage is not established; isolated neurologic reports do not define most cases.
Congenital urethral obstruction damages bladder and kidneys. Associated UTIs are separate infections; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%.
Wilms/urinary phenotype, aniridia and obesity define syndrome; intellectual disability 3/3. Cap excludes exostoses reported in 1/2.
LAM proliferation causes cystic lung destruction and pleural disease; associated renal angiomyolipoma is a separate neoplasm.
Gangrenous oral infection destroys facial skin; facial bone destruction is part of the defining disease process.
Extragonadal germ-cell tumor of the mediastinum; this site is outside the specified axes, and lung or other covered-organ origin is not established.
Defined by abnormal cavernous blood-vessel spaces; anatomic sites vary, and the vascular lesion does not itself establish blood-cell or coagulation disease.
